metadata.title: Digitale vaardigheden in het tweede jaar secundair onderwijs in Vlaanderen: Resultaten van ICILS 2023 in internationaal vergelijkend perspectief

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: ICILS 2023 uses a multi-stage sampling design with stratification at the school level and random selection of classes and students within selected schools. The report describes that non-response and exclusions are handled to maintain representativeness, including the use of (weighted) response rates and the correction of underrepresented groups via weights during analyses. For the Vlaamse sample, the report reports a combined (weighted) response rate meeting IEA criteria and notes that weights are used to ensure that groups excluded or underrepresented due to non-response contribute proportionally to population estimates. The report also explains that standard errors and 95% confidence intervals are computed around means, consistent with complex survey uncertainty; however, the specific weight variable name is not provided in the excerpt.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This brochure reports ICILS results based on IRT-scaled proficiency scores and IEA-defined skill levels for the two cognitive domains (CIL and CT), rather than documenting Plausible Values (PV) handling procedures. Because the excerpt does not provide the PV or missing-data strategy details (e.g., PV generation/combining rules or explicit missing-data imputation/deletion rules), the missing-data handling is treated as not reported. This is a reporting gap for methodological transparency, since large-scale assessments typically require explicit handling of missing responses and non-response.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The Vlaamse sample is drawn as a probability sample of schools offering the second year of secondary education, with stratification by educational track offerings and school network, and checks for representativeness using an educational disadvantage indicator (OKI). Schools are excluded if they offer only excluded educational forms/types (BuSO) or have fewer than ten students in the second year; additionally, each selected school has one or two reserve schools used when participation is not possible. Within participating schools, 1–2 classes are randomly selected (with an additional class selected if the chosen class has too few students). Students are excluded only in exceptional cases: physical or severe mental/emotional limitations preventing test participation, or non-Dutch-speaking students when they have at most one year in Dutch-language education and insufficient language proficiency for reliable assessment. Non-response is primarily due to absence (e.g., illness) or students leaving school; the report states that 2.7% of students were removed in the sampling process and 6.7% of selected students did not respond.

data.outcome_summary: This ICILS 2023 Vlaanderen brochure reports descriptive and comparative results for students in the second year of secondary education (international Grade 8 equivalent) in two cognitive domains: Computer and Information Literacy (CIL) and Computational Thinking (CT). The assessment is administered in a computer-based environment with multiple test modules (four modules total per student: two for CIL and two for CT), and scores are produced using IRT-based scaling to place students on a common proficiency scale across different test forms. The report uses IEA-defined international benchmarks: a reference mean of 500 and standard deviation of 100 (anchored to earlier ICILS cycles) and four skill levels for each domain, plus reporting of percentiles (e.g., P90–P10 spread). For Vlaanderen, the mean CIL score is about 510.6 (higher than the ICILS 2023 average of 476.2) and the mean CT score is about 509.1 (higher than the ICILS 2023 average of 483.1). The brochure also reports relationships between proficiency and background/context variables using a “net model” approach with control variables, and it emphasizes representativeness via IEA response-rate criteria and complex-survey uncertainty (standard errors and 95% confidence intervals). Limitations include that the excerpt does not specify PV handling or missing-data procedures, and the reported “net model” results are not framed as causal effects.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a descriptive large-scale assessment results brochure rather than an empirical machine-learning paper. As such, there are no ML algorithms trained or evaluated, and therefore ml_techniques are left empty. The excerpt also does not provide PV-specific or missing-data handling documentation, and the report focuses on IRT-scaled proficiency reporting and benchmark comparisons rather than on PV-based modeling transparency.
